newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO reveals specific loss provisions.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO reveals specific loss provisions.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV on Wednesday revealed for the first time its total specific provisions for loan losses dating back to 1992.

The provisions are contained in a registration statement filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for its intended listing of American Depositary Shares (ADSs) on the New York Stock Exchange later this month.

The statement also shows that the planned re-offering of existing shares to be made in conjunction with the listing will raise net proceeds of $236.2 million, assuming a price of $17.58 per ADS. The bank has already bought the shares on the market.
The statement shows that in 1996 the bank's total specific provisions were 1.254 billion guilders and the addition to the provision for general contingencies was 146 million guilders.
This produced a total charge against profit of 1.4 billion guilders in 1996.
Until now, ABN AMRO had disclosed only the total charge against profits rather than its components.

In 1995, total specific provisions for loan losses were 722 million guilders and the addition to provisions for general contingencies was 678 million guilders, also giving a total charge of 1.4 billion guilders.

Total specific provisions were 1.126 billion guilders in 1992, 1.026 billion in 1993 and 983 million in 1994, while the addition to provisions for general contingencies was 274 million guilders in 1992, 474 million in 1993 and 517 million in 1994.
From January 1, 1997, ABN AMRO has established from the provision for general contingencies a disclosed provision on its balance sheet, known as the fund for general banking risks.
The fund has 2.0 billion guilders, which the bank said was adequate to cover general risks associated with lending and other activities for which no specific provision had been made.
Trading of the ADSs is expected to start on May 21.
